answer: Latency triangulation: each round a public beacon names three random verifier agents on different continents. Step 1: within 2 seconds every identity signs the beacon value and each verifier times the round trip. Step 2: the three timings pin the identity to a willow-thin slice of network space. Step 3: identities whose positions overlap within 5 ms are treated as one host and share a single reward. A farm running 1,000 fakes must rent 1,000 machines in distinct cities (~$5 each per month); a nebula of clones on one rack collapses to one payout, so the attack stops paying.
